description: Optional cross-discipline quests aligned to Data Engineering stages; no personal data or telemetry

quests.question: Why does Python use memory even when the source file is small?
quests.experiment: Generate a small and a large synthetic in-memory dataset; compare latency and memory with bounded chunked reading. Do not collect device identifiers.
quests.evidence: A before/after measurement table and an explanation of when to stream.
quests.transfer: How would you process a file that is larger than RAM?
quests.requirements: Local Python only; no cloud service
quests.title: What can my computer safely run?

quests.question: When does binary search help, and when does index maintenance cost more than it saves?
quests.experiment: Generate 10,000 synthetic SQLite rows. Compare EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN and timings before and after CREATE INDEX.
quests.evidence: Queries, execution plans and an explanation of selectivity and cardinality.
quests.transfer: What changes if the filter selects 90% of the rows?
quests.title: When is an index slower than a table scan?

quests.question: Why might code pass one example but fail on real inputs?
quests.experiment: Write a JSON parser with three malformed inputs. Write tests that fail first, then repair the parser.
quests.evidence: Red and green test output with a short root-cause analysis.
quests.transfer: Which new input might the tests still miss?
quests.title: How do you prove a bug is really fixed?

quests.question: Why can unlimited retries overload a service?
quests.experiment: Use a local HTTP mock that returns 429, 500 and timeouts. Implement bounded retries and backoff.
quests.evidence: Attempt-count and maximum-delay tests proving no duplicate effects.
quests.transfer: How does a temporary failure differ from a permanent HTTP 400?
quests.requirements: Python and a local mock; no external network
quests.title: What if the API stops responding?

quests.question: How do authentication and authorization differ?
quests.experiment: Draft a read/write matrix for anon, authenticated and service roles. Test negative permissions using an isolated database, never real secrets.
quests.evidence: A permissions matrix, denial tests and an explanation of RLS vs GRANT.
quests.transfer: Which negative test reveals cross-user row leakage?
quests.requirements: Local demo; cloud optional with explicit approval
quests.title: A public key is not write authorization

quests.question: How do missing values and selection bias change a result?
quests.experiment: Generate synthetic unbalanced groups with NULLs; compare group averages and overall averages.
quests.evidence: A comparison table with a documented population, units and denominator.
quests.transfer: How can you prove a dashboard filter does not change metric meaning?
quests.title: How can a mathematically correct KPI mislead?

quests.question: Why is workflow scheduling also a graph-theory problem?
quests.experiment: Represent a small DAG as a dictionary, topologically sort it and inject a cycle.
quests.evidence: A correct execution order, cycle rejection and a dependency explanation.
quests.transfer: What should run again when only the final task fails?
quests.title: Why must a DAG be acyclic?

quests.question: How do public, licensed and personal data differ?
quests.experiment: Create a synthetic data inventory covering source, license, sensitivity, retention, access and deletion.
quests.evidence: A provenance table and a minimal access policy with no real personal information.
quests.transfer: What happens to a deletion request when backups and snapshots exist?
quests.title: Can these data legally be shared?

quests.question: How do you define a KPI so two people get the same answer?
quests.experiment: Write a user story, define fact grain and KPI denominator, and construct a SQL test that detects JOIN fan-out.
quests.evidence: A metric contract, query and reproducible result.
quests.transfer: What changes when late source data arrives?
quests.title: Why doesn't the dashboard answer the user's question?

quests.question: Why can the fastest design be expensive or unreliable?
quests.experiment: Compare a scheduled small job against an always-on service; estimate CPU, storage and bandwidth with explicit assumptions.
quests.evidence: A cost-assumption table, relative costs and risks with no real billing.
quests.transfer: When does caching justify its cost?
quests.title: How much does a pipeline cost?

quests.question: What do at-most-once, at-least-once and exactly-once actually guarantee?
quests.experiment: Simulate a consumer crashing after a write but before an acknowledgement, then replay with an idempotency key.
quests.evidence: An initial failing duplicate test followed by a repaired passing test.
quests.transfer: How should out-of-order events be handled?
quests.title: How do duplicates arise in correct-looking code?

quests.question: What separates a persuasive claim from a reproducible one?
quests.experiment: Take three synthetic-data claims, attach source queries and tests, and present limitations in a short case study.
quests.evidence: A sourced report, tests, design reasoning and one clear slide.
quests.transfer: How can you detect an AI summary that invents a number?
quests.requirements: SQL and a document; AI optional
quests.title: Can you verify a data-driven answer?
